title: Migrate worker lease to hybrid locks and signal-driven throttler
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current worker orchestration relies on a single Redis-based lease model for multi-tenant queues. This has surfaced issues: long tail lease renewals when Redis operations stall, noisy failover during transient network blips, and a blunt global backpressure approach that penalizes healthy tenants when one tenant spikes. We also rely on a legacy redis client (v3.x) which has edge-case retry behavior that interacts poorly with our renewal loop.

Goal: Replace the single-source lease + global shedder with a hybrid lease model (ephemeral Redis locks + Kafka consumer-group affinity) and a signal-driven throttler (token-bucket style scheduler driven by runtime telemetry). This should reduce failover churn, allow per-tenant adaptive concurrency, and eliminate a class of phantom renewals. The ticket covers design, dependency upgrade, implementation, canary rollout, and observability.

Design summary: 
- Hybrid lease: keep fast ephemeral Redis locks for short-lived leadership and heartbeats, but use Kafka consumer-group assignment as the canonical owner for shards when available. On restart/rebalance, Kafka assignment is authoritative; Redis locks act as a low-latency hint and a short-term handoff mechanism.
- Lease semantics: introduce a lease state machine with states: "hinted", "claimed", "confirmed". Renewals use jittered intervals, and a configurable grace window prevents immediate reclaims.
- Signal-driven throttler: per-tenant token buckets where refill rates are derived from live SLO/latency windows and recent token consumption. A central controller publishes refill deltas via an internal control channel (gRPC topic) that workers subscribe to; local enforcement is lock-free and bounded.
- Retry semantics: move from fixed global retry windows to per-message idempotency keys + exponential backoff with bounded jitter and retry budget counters per-tenant. Introduce a small persistent retry queue for messages that exceed a tenant's concurrency budget but are still retryable.
- Dependency upgrades: bump redis client to 4.x (notes below), upgrade kafka client to latest stable, and pin circuit-breaker lib to 2.1.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Complexity vs stability: hybrid model increases complexity in codepath but measurably reduces rebalance churn in spiky scenarios (see bench notes).
- Control plane dependency: signaling requires a lightweight control channel; we chose gRPC pub/sub to avoid adding Redis pub/sub coupling. This introduces an operational dependency on the control plane but enables low-latency global adjustments.
- Consistency: Kafka assignment is authoritative to avoid split-brain. In edge cases where Kafka metadata lags, Redis hinting prevents unnecessary work duplication.

Migration plan: 
1) Implement lease state machine behind feature flag; keep current renewal code untouched until canary completes.
2) Deploy upgraded redis client on a small subset of workers and validate lease ops and retry behavior.
3) Enable hybrid mode for a single non-critical customer shard and monitor metrics.
4) Gradually expand and enable signal-driven throttler with conservative default refill profiles.
5) Remove old global shedder and legacy renewal loop once stability confirmed.

Acceptance criteria: 
- No increase in user-facing errors for canary shards over 48h (error rate <= baseline + 1%).
- 20% reduction in worker churn (restarts/reclaims) under synthetic spike tests.
- Per-tenant P50/P95 concurrency aligns with token-bucket targets within 10% for steady-state workloads.
- Dashboards show retry budget usage and backpressure signals; alerts fire if a tenant hits 90% of retry budget for >10m.

Instrumentation and observability: 
- New metrics: worker.lease.state{state,shard}, worker.lease.renewal_latency_ms, throttler.tokens.available{tenant}, throttler.refill.delta, retry.budget.remaining{tenant}.
- Trace additions: mark lease handoff traces and control-channel events.
- Dashboards: "Hybrid Lease Overview" + "Per-tenant Concurrency". Links in 'links' field below.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Redis client upgrade surfaced a bug with pipelined renewals in v3.x -> upgrade to 4.x and add defensive circuit-breaker wrapping renew calls. CI spike tests added.
- Control-plane outtage could stall refill updates; local token buckets continue operating at last-known refill rate and fallback to conservative defaults.
- Kafka rebalances could cause short double-processing windows if Redis hints haven't expired; tuned grace window to avoid duplicates and added idempotency checks at message consumer path.

Artifacts: design doc, benchmark results, PRs linked below.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Patel: Completed spike and prototype of lease state machine. Microbenchmarks show reduced tail on lease-renew ops when using hinting (p50 down ~8ms). Identified flaky pipelined renew behavior in redis-client v3.7.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Gonzalez: Implemented hybrid lease core and local token-bucket enforcement. Wrote unit tests for state transitions and grace window handling. Discovered a race in consumer rebalance callback ordering; added a short wait-for-confirmation path.

2026-03-06 - Lina Zhou (SRE): Ran synthetic tenant spike test. Worker churn decreased by ~18% on canary nodes. Observability gaps: missing throttler.refill.delta metric in early runs — fixed in PR #4021.
2026-03-08 - Security review: Quick review done; no sensitive data flows introduced by control channel. Marking security_review_required=false. Full ERS not needed for now.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Gonzalez: Canary expansion to 5 more shards behind feature flag. Preparing PR for redis client upgrade and smoke tests. Next: add dashboard panels and alerting rules before broader rollout.
